top_categories.workout_context: 13,688ft of climbing makes aerobic ceiling relevant when the grade or pace changes. VO2max work supports those hard moments; sustained climbing and conservative pacing remain the spine.
146ft/mi signals a climbing-heavy course. Sustained sub-threshold and threshold work builds the steady power needed without turning the opening climb into the day’s hardest effort.
At La Vaujany Cyclosportive, changes in grade or pace can lift effort above threshold before it settles again. Over-unders train that transition while you keep riding.

Road-specific control matters at La Vaujany Cyclosportive. Practice on mixed terrain: use smooth gear and cadence changes, accelerate deliberately out of corners, and settle quickly back into sustainable power for 93 miles.
Race-pace efforts that mimic La Vaujany Cyclosportive's demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before June.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of La Vaujany Cyclosportive. Train it until it feels boring.
13,688ft of climbing on grades that change every minute. You need to switch from seated to standing without losing rhythm.
At mile 60 of 93, glycogen is gone. This workout teaches your body to produce watts on fumes.
Every hard session works better with a bigger aerobic base. At 93 miles, base fitness is the difference between racing and surviving.
Brief efforts above sustainable power can come from grade changes, positioning, or closing a gap at La Vaujany Cyclosportive. Train them without letting those efforts derail the longer pacing plan.
Low-cadence force work supports 13,688ft of climbing when the grade lowers cadence. Practice controlled torque while preserving good form.
Steeper ramps, positioning, or pace changes on mixed terrain can demand short hard efforts. Practice them without compromising the sustained work that defines the course.

race_overlay.nutrition: Target 60–80g carbs/hour for La Vaujany Cyclosportive’s 93 miles. Start fueling within the first 30 minutes — early fueling prevents late-race collapse. Bonking at mile 60 is a nutrition failure, not a fitness failure.
race_overlay.altitude: La Vaujany Cyclosportive includes meaningful altitude exposure. Reduced oxygen availability can affect sustainable power, pacing, and recovery. Use a conservative upper-mountain pacing plan, test any travel or acclimatization strategy before the event, and plan layers for changing conditions. Do not begin iron or other supplements without clinician-guided testing.
race_overlay.terrain: The course profile at La Vaujany Cyclosportive rewards specific practice. Include regular rides on mixed terrain to build confidence.

pack_summary: This 10-workout pack focuses on VO2max, TT Threshold, and Over Under to prepare you for 93 miles of mixed terrain in Vaujany, Isère, France.
